decision_target: Whether Gift Aid can be claimed on the £260 payment received from Robyn Ellis on 4 February 2026

atoms.proposition: The claiming organisation is recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes by HMRC
atoms.entity_scope: the charity run by the customer

atoms.proposition: The donation was made by an individual (not a company or other entity)
The donor paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in the relevant tax year as the amount the charity wishes to claim in Gift Aid on this donation
atoms.entity_scope: Robyn Ellis in the tax year containing 4 February 2026

atoms.proposition: The donor has made a Gift Aid declaration giving the charity permission to claim Gift Aid on this donation
atoms.entity_scope: Robyn Ellis in relation to the £260 payment

atoms.proposition: The £260 payment is not a payment for goods or services supplied by the charity or CASC, and is not made because the charity or CASC bought goods or services from the donor
The donation was not made through Payroll Giving
The donor does not receive a 'benefit' in connection with this donation that exceeds the permitted limit
atoms.entity_scope: Robyn Ellis in relation to the £260 payment

atoms.proposition: The donation is not a donation of shares
The donation is not made from a charity card or by means of a voucher (e.g. a CAF voucher)

scope_issues: The customer also receives regular monthly direct-debit donations and other one-off donations; each of those transactions would require a separate Gift Aid eligibility assessment and is not covered by this representation, which is scoped solely to the £260 payment of 4 February 2026.
The separate £20 cash gift from Robyn Ellis at the December collection event is explicitly noted as a different transaction and is outside the scope of this assessment.
limitations: The passages do not specify the precise monetary threshold for a donor 'benefit' under E11, so the exact limit cannot be stated here.
The passages do not define what counts as a 'benefit' in detail, leaving room for ambiguity in applying a7 to advertising or promotional arrangements.

Whether the £260 constitutes a genuine donation or a payment for advertising services (newsletter link and homepage feature placement) is a factual question critical to a5 but the policy passages do not provide further guidance on how to characterise mixed or disputed payments.
The passages do not address how to treat a payment that was internally relabelled as a donation after the fact, nor the significance of no invoice having been raised.
Robyn Ellis's tax position (a3) and whether a Gift Aid declaration exists (a4) are explicitly noted as unchecked in the scenario.
